Undergraduate Courses in Anthropology

General students who major in anthropology must elect the following courses: Anthropology 101*/102* and at least four additional courses (or half course equivalents) in Anthropology. Students who pursue on Honours Programme in Anthropology must take Anthropology 101*/102*, a theory course at the 400 level, and at least eight other courses (or half course equivalents) in Anthropology. Students may pursue a joint honours programme with the permission of Anthropology and the other discipline involved. Oorinarily this would mean taking seven anthropology courses (including Anthropology 101*/102*, and a theory course at the 400 level, seven courses in the other discipline and eight electives. Requirements of the second department may lead to some alteration of the formula. Students taking a combined honours programme should consult with advisers in both disciplines to obtain a programme tailored to their needs.

courses.label: ANTH 101
courses.title: Origins of Man and Culture
paras: An introductory course in Physical Anthropology and Archaeology. Lectures on living and fossil primates, the fossil primates, the fossil evidence for the origins and development of man, modern races, and archaeological evidence for the origins and development of culture.

courses.label: ANTH 102
courses.title: Cultural and Social Anthropology
paras: An introductory course on the nature of culture. Data are presented on several primitive cultures.

courses.label: ANTH 210
courses.title: Primitive Mythology
paras: An introduction to the study of the beliefs and practices of primitive peoples about the world of nature and of man. The course will deal with the religious and related systems of selected primitive peoples. Readings will reflect these accounts in the ethnographic literature. Prerequisites: 102 or permission of instructor.
$29 Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: ANTH 218
courses.title: North American Archaeology Paleo-Indian and Archaic
paras: A survey of the earliest known cultures in North America. Prerequistes: 101 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 219
courses.title: North American Archaeology — the later cultures
paras: A survey of North American cultures from the emergence of food production as a major factor in cultural development to the advent of Europeans. 10] or permission of the instructor. Prerequisites.

courses.label: ANTH 220
courses.title: Old World Prehistory The Food Procuring Phases
paras: A survey of the development of culture, from the beginnings of tool making to the transition to agriculture. Primary attention to sequences from Africa, Western Asia, and Europe. Comparative attention to the nonagriculture peoples of recent times. 101 or permission of the instructor. Prerequisites.

courses.label: ANTH 221
courses.title: Old World Prehistory The Food Producing Phases
paras: Examination of the transition to an economy based on food production, the spread of food producing economics, the rise of civilization in the Near East to the early literate periods. Consideration of later prehistoric developments in Africa, Asia and Europe. 101 or permission of the instructor. Prerequisites.

courses.label: ANTH 227
courses.title: Peoples of Africa
paras: - A survey of the cultures and societies of sub-Saharan Africa. An emphasis will be placed upon the ethnographic present. Prerequisites: 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 228
courses.title: Peoples of the Pacific
paras: A comparative ethnological survey of selected indigenous societies in the Pacific region. 102 or permission of the instructor Prerequisites.

courses.label: ANTH 230
courses.title: (Art 216*) Primitive Art
paras: A study of Paleolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic world art, aspects of Bronze Age Europe, Asia, and the Near East, the art of the African continent, the North and South American Indians in pre-Columbian and colonial times, and Australian-Oceania, together with related fields such as folk art, naive art and child art.

courses.label: ANTH 233
courses.title: Eskimo Cultures
paras: Eskimo cultures of Alaska, Canada and Greenland from the time of European and Asian contact to the present. Administrative systems imposed on the Eskimo will be analysed and compared, as will the contemporary problems these communities face today. Prerequisites: 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 234
courses.title: North American Indians
paras: A survey of the cultures of the native peoples of Canada and the United States at the time of contact with Eurupean Civilization. Emphasis will be placed upon such aspects as cultural ecology, tribal socio-political organization and nativistic reactions to Europeans. Prerequisites: Anthropology 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 235
courses.title: Contemporary Canadian Indian Scene
paras: An analysis of present day Canadian Indian politics, economics, social organization, education and religion. The Indian Act and its implementation by the Indian Affairs Department will be studied in view of assessing its role in maintaining Indian cultures. Comparative data will be drawn from the literature of Indians in the United States. Prerequisites: Anthropology 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 236J
courses.title: Social and Cultural Change in South East Asia
paras: This course analyses the traditional social structure as well as changes in social, economic and cultural spheres in selected Asian countries. Historical perspective will be emphasized. Current topics such as land reform, the consequent changes, or changing values in the traditional societies will also be discussed. Prerequisite: Sociology 101* or Anthropology 101*, 102*.

courses.label: ANTH 238
courses.title: Caribbean Society
paras: A survey of Carribean society in which particular attention will be devoted to an analysis of the historical, cultural and socioeconomic background of selected representative Caribbean societies, within the general framework of the continuing process of acculturation in this area. Prerequisites; Anthropology 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 247
courses.title: Urban Anthropology
paras: Approaches to the study of urban centres as undertaken by anthropologists. Selected topics such as urban social networks, the urbanization of non-western societies, and the culture of poverty will be pursued. Prerequisites: 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 248
courses.title: Peasant Society
paras: A survey course with data taken from Latin America, Europe, India, Southeast Asia. Included will be a consideration of different types of peasant societies, the relationship of peasants to urban areas, and the effects of modernization on peasant society.

courses.label: ANTH 260
courses.title: Human Evolution
paras: Data, methods and theory in the study of the origin and evolution of man. Emphasis will be on the fossil evidence. Prerequisites: 101 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 261
courses.title: Primate Behaviour
paras: An introduction to the behaviour of non-human primates with emphasis on the relevance to the origin of man.

courses.label: ANTH 270
courses.title: (Music 270*G) The Folk Music of Europe and North America
paras: Countries to be discussed: British Isles, France, Germany, the Balkans and Eastern Europe, including the Ukraine and Russia; Canada and the USA through Library of Congress record albums, Czechoslovakia, Greece, Hungary, Rumania.

courses.label: ANTH 280
courses.title: Language and Culture
paras: The importance of language in culture. Language is examined as a vehicle of culture (a linguistic code as a device for communication), as a mirror for culture (lexical and semantic aspects), and as a tool of society (uses and functions of language). Illustrations will be from a variety of languages. Prerequisites: 102*, 234 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 283
courses.title: Phonology for Non-Linguists
paras: Devising adequate writing systems for unwritten languages. The class will simulate field sessions, with an informant who speaks an unfamiliar language.

courses.label: ANTH 285
courses.title: Introduction to Structural Linguistics
paras: A general introduction to structural linguistics. A survey of linguistic approaches to the analysis and description of language.
Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: ANTH 310
courses.title: Ethnology of North American Sub-Arctic
paras: An analysis of Northern Athabaskan and Algonkian Social organisation and culture from earliest European contact, the fur trade periods to the period of modern, concentrated village life. Emphasis will be upon culture change and adaptation in a theoretical framework of cultural ecology and historical development. Prerequisites: 102*, 234 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 330
courses.title: Cultural Ecology 42J Introduction to the Study of Acculturation
paras: This course will study the interrelations between societies and their environments. It will cover both the cultural relations to the natural surroundings and community organization. 101* and 102* or permission of instructor. Prerequisites.

A study of culture contact and the cultural changes that result, pursued through a study of representative non-European peoples in different parts of the world including their indigenous cultures and the problems of adapting themselves to the modern world. Prerequisites: Anthropology 101*, 102* or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 353
courses.title: Primitive Social Organization
paras: A study of primitive social structure. Systems of Kinship and marriage, residence patterns, and family structure are discussed. Prerequisites: 102* or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 355J
courses.title: Ethnic and Cultural Pluralism in World Perspective
paras: A survey of representative plural societies of the world, including an analysis of the historical background and genesis of ethnic and cultural pluralism in these societies. An attempt will be made to establish the relevance of the concept of plural society for some national societies not usually recognized as such on the basis of the nature of some of their major continuing internal social problems. Considerable attention will also be given to race and ethnicity and the major role these two factors play in plural societies. Prerequisites: Anthropology 101*, 102* or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 356
courses.title: Comparative Economic Organization
paras: A discussion of the alternative means of organizing economic activity, focused primarily on non-market societies. Prerequisites: 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 357
courses.title: Hunting and Gathering Cultures of North America
paras: Archaeological and ethnological data on various prehistoric and historic groups are presented. Emphasis is on hunting and gathering cultures as a distinct type. Prerequisites: 101* and 102*, or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 359
courses.title: Political Anthropology
paras: The study of political behaviour in both state and non-state society. A comparative approach will be used with a thorough examination of the political systems of selected societies. Prerequisites: 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 360
courses.title: Variability in Human Populations
paras: Study of physical variation and its causes in contemporary human populations. Prerequisites: 260* or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 361
courses.title: Behaviour and Evolution
paras: Analysis of the relationship between behaviour and natural selection in human evolution. Attention will be paid to theory as well as data from fossil evidence and other sources. Prerequisites: 260* or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 362
courses.title: New World Civilization
paras: Problems in cultural dynamics will be considered as exemplified in the rise and effects of the civilizations of Meso and South America. Data are provided primarily by the archaeological record. Prerequisites: 101* or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 370
courses.title: Ethnographic Field Methods
paras: Traditional and recently developed approaches to ethnographic field work are explored. The problems the worker faces in the field, and possible solutions to them, are discussed. Some effort will be made to develop field technique in simulated and/or real field situations. Prerequisites: 102* or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 371
courses.title: Archaeological Field Methods
paras: Data gathering techniques will be studied and applied in fieldwork on both constructed and natural archaeological sites. Prerequisites; 101* or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 372
courses.title: Archaeological Techniques
paras: Methods of gathering, processing and interpreting archaeological data will be studied. Limited excavations will be followed by laboratory analysis of collected materials. Prerequisite: 101* or permission of instructor. This course will ordinarily be offered in the fall term. Students cannot receive credit for both 371 and 372*.

courses.label: ANTH 375
courses.title: Ethnohistory
paras: Ethnohistory as a method of research in which historical data are used in the solution of anthropological problems. General consideration will be given to Indians of the Americas, with special attention to Indians of Canada. Prerequisites: 102*, 234 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 381
courses.title: Semology
paras: A linguistic approach to the study of meanings expressed in the grammatical systems and lexical sets of particular languages. Prerequisites: Anthropology 280* or 285.

courses.label: ANTH 388
courses.title: Applied Anthropology 390, 391*, 392, 393*, 395*, 397* Reading in Anthropology
paras: The technical and ethical aspects of directed culture change will be examined. Prerequisites: 370* or permission of the instructor.
Guided reading in a selected portion of the anthropological literature. Prerequisites: Anthropology major and permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 401
courses.title: Seminar in the Literature of Social and Cultural Anthropology
paras: Seminar in the literature of Social and Cultural Anthropology. Intensive reading and discussion of classic studies in ethnography. Prerequisites: 102* or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 420
courses.title: Social and Cultural Change
paras: An analysis of contemporary thought on culture contact and cultural evolution. The concepts to be explored might include integration, assimilation, conflict, nativistic reactions, general and specific evolution. Prerequisites: Anthropology 102* or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 449
courses.title: Honours Seminar
paras: Seminar on selected contemporary issues in anthropology. Open only to Honours Anthropology students.

courses.label: ANTH 451
courses.title: The Formative Years of Cultural Theory
paras: A survey of the history of cultural theory from 1850 to 1940. Prerequisites: Anthropology 101%, 102*.

courses.label: SOC 452
courses.title: Contemporary Cultural Theory
paras: A survey of cultural theory from post World War II to the present. Prerequisites: Anthropology 101*, 102*.

courses.label: SOC 458
courses.title: Archaeological Theory
paras: A seminar on selected topics in archaeological theory. Prerequisites: Anthropology 102* and an additional half course in archaeology or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: SOC 460
courses.title: Advanced Physical Anthropology
paras: An examination of selected topics of current research interest in physical anthropology. Students will be encouraged to undertake guided research projects. Prerequisites: Anthropology 260*, 360* and permission of the instructor.

courses.label: SOC 480
courses.title: Theoretical Approaches to Linguistic Description
paras: Different theoretical approaches — stratificational, transformational and signals grammer, one approach to be emphasized during each offering. Prerequisites: Anthropology 285 or English 375.

courses.label: SOC 499
courses.title: Honours Essay Note 1 Note 2 Note 3
paras: Directed reading and research in a selected area of anthropological inquiry. Open only to Honours Anthropology students.
Undergraduate Courses in Sociology

General students who major in Sociology must elect the following courses: Sociology 101*, a half course in sociological methods, a half course in sociological theory, and three and one half full courses (or equivalent half courses) in Sociology. Students are strongly encouraged to elect Sociology 202*, although this is not required. An Honours programme in Sociology is a pre-professional degree, so the specific requirements have been formulated in the light of professional and graduate school requirements. Students are reminded that Sociology is now accepted as a high school teaching subject in Ontario. Potential high school teachers should keep informed of the requirements for teaching Sociology in high schools. Students may elect Honours Sociology (Canadian Studies) by fulfilling the requirements listed under Canadian Studies in this calendar. The student is reminded that an Honours or a major programme in Sociology is intended to provide a liberal arts education. Students are encouraged to avoid excessive concentration in Sociology, and to elect courses in a variety of social sciences, humanities, modern languages, as well as in other Faculties.

courses.label: SOC 101
courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
paras: An introduction to the basic concepts and frames of reference of sociological investigation and interpretation. Topics for analysis will include communities, associations and institutions, classes and status groups, crowds and publics, social processes, and social change. Special attention is given to Canadian society. Not open to students who have taken Soc. 141*. 2 lectures, Fall and Winter terms.

courses.label: SOC 141
courses.title: The Sociological Enterprise
paras: A survey of what sociologists do, with an introduction to rudimentary sociological methods. Readings from a variety of sources giving an account of the thinking behind sociological projects of small and large scale. Not open to students who have taken Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 200
courses.title: Canadian Society in Comparative Perspective
paras: Analysis of Canadian society: its institutions such as family and religion, and social processes, such as integration, stratification and demography, with comparisons to other industrialized societies. Prerequisite: Soc, 101* 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 202
courses.title: Sociological Statistics
paras: A first course in sociological statistics; sampling, central tendency, probability, co-variance, as illustrated in specifically sociological data. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 205
courses.title: Social Problems
paras: An examination of cultural forces that create social problems and failures in personal and institutional adjustments. Specific attention is paid to the problems of emotional disturbance, addictions, deliquency and crime in Canadian society. No prerequisite. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 208
courses.title: Elementary Problems in (non-participant) Field Observation
paras: Sociological concepts and ideas are put into use in systematic observation, recording, and analysis of structures and processes related to particular social institutions. For example, courts that are open to the public enable us to combine theoretical learning about the systems of jurisprudence and jurisdiction on the one hand and their application in particular courts on the other. Relevant readings, observational records, and resulting methodological or theoretical questions will be discussed in seminars and tutorials. Prerequisite: Soc. 101" and permission of the instructor. 2 hour seminar, 4 hour lab., Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 209
courses.title: Advanced Problems in (non-participant) Field Observation
paras: A continuation of Sociology 208*. Here instruction concentrates on the use of observational data in the formulation of questions about the structures and dynamics that have been and are currently being observed and recorded. A satisfactory grade in Soc. 208* is required for admission to Sociology 209*. Prerequisite: Soc. 208* 2 hour seminar, 4 hour lab, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 210
courses.title: Introductory Social Psychology
paras: Basic concepts in the interdisciplinary field of social psychology; approached from the perspectives of social influence. Individualistic, interpersonal, and group-based strategies for influencing the behaviour of others are examined. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* or Psych. 101* 3 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 212
courses.title: Interpersonal Relations
paras: The contribution of social organization to interpersonal processes. Consideration of some “theories” of social interaction. The social system approach to the problem of personal and interpersonal control. 101* or Psych. 101* Prerequisite: Soc. 3 lectures, Winter term.
Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: SOC 215
courses.title: Sociology of Women
paras: A comparative analysis of women’s roles in past and present with selected cross-cultural data. Assessment of the present situation. Subjective factors: socialization of women into “women’s” roles, internalization of role expectations by women, perpetuation of stereotypes and symbolic expression of differential worth of men and women. Objective factors: the legal situation, women on the labor market, the “sex revolution”, and the women’s liberation movement. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, I discussion, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 218
courses.title: Sociology of Adolescence
paras: The social definitions of adolescence in cross-cultural and historical perspective. Social roles of adolescence in the institutional structures of urban industrial societies with special emphasis on the family, education, and the economy. The relationship of adolescents’ social roles to processes of social change and stability. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 240
courses.title: Collective Behaviour
paras: The sociological analysis of the behaviour of crowds, mobs, publics, and related phenomena and their relationships to social organization and social change. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 241
courses.title: Social Movements
paras: The sociological analysis of varieties of social movements and their relationships to social organization and social change. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 250
courses.title: Crime and Society 51* Ethnic and Racial Relations
paras: An analysis and criticism of the major theories of criminal behaviour. Emphasis is given to the relationship between social structure and criminal behaviour; types of criminal behaviour such as drug addiction; statistics and contemporary research. Special attention is given to Canadian data. A sound knowledge of sociological concepts is advisable. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Fall term.
Relations between different racial and cultural groups; analysis of majority-minority group status with special reference to Canada. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 252
courses.title: Juvenile Delinquency
paras: A systematic analysis and criticism is presented of biological, psychological, psychoanalytical and sociological theories of juvenile delinquency. Attention is given to statistics and contemporary research with special emphasis on the distribution and types of delinquent subcultures. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 3 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 261
courses.title: Population Issues
paras: The study of population as an area of sociological investigation; population size, composition, and distribution; population trends and problems. No prerequisites. 3 lectures, Fail term.

courses.label: SOC 262
courses.title: Canadian Population
paras: Study of the basic demographic processes in the population of Canada. Demographic implications for selected social institutions. Use of Canadian enumeration and registration data. No prerequisites. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 265
courses.title: Social Structure of East Asia: China and Japan
paras: An analysis of the social structure and stratification of East Asia in terms of class, status, prestige, rank and function with especial consideration given to the question of class formation in Japan and attempted class elimination in China. No prerequisites. 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 270
courses.title: Communication
paras: An analysis of the role of language and other symbol systems in social interaction; the interplay between communication and the social system, the formation of attitudes through language; social and individual disorders as caused by, and reflected in, the breakdown in the communication process. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 280
courses.title: Social Organization of Animal Societies
paras: The social behaviour of various species of animals will be examined and compared. The main emphasis will be on exploring the nature of social behaviour and gaining further understanding of human societies by comparing them with others. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 290
courses.title: Introduction to Qualitative Social Thought
paras: Lectures, readings and discussion of selected original sources both Eastern and Western which attempt to define and evaluate the relation of the individual to society, and sgciety to nature and cosmos, as expressed in classical as well as in later documents. Topics will include the mythological world-view; the emergence of an ordered social cosmos in Greece, the Middle East and China; and the response to these issues in the social thought of Europe. No prerequisite. 2 hours, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 301
courses.title: Urban Sociology
paras: The comparative study of urbanization as a process; the culture and social organization of cities, urban problems; special attention is given to industrial cities of Canada, with comparative reference to the principal industrial cities of Western societies. Prerequisite: Soc. 10]* 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 308
courses.title: Elementary Problems in (participant) Field Observation
paras: Here, as in Sociology 208* and 209* concepts and ideas are to be put to use. Now, however, the observational setting is complicated by making the observer part of it. Participant observation may take place in formal organization settings such as hospitals, factories, or schools, or in informal association settings involving voluntary associations and groups. Reading, recording and seminar discussion supplement the field experience. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* and permission of the instructor. 2 hour seminar, 4 hour lab., Fall term.
Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: SOC 309
courses.title: Advanced Problems in (participant) Field Observation 10* Seminar in Group Dynamics
paras: A continuation of Sociology 308*. Here instruction concentrates on the use of observational data in the formulation of questions about the structures and dynamics that have been and are currently being observed and recorded. A satisfactory grade in Sociology 308* is required for admission to Soc. 309*. Prerequisite: Soc. 308* 2 hour seminar, 4 hour lab, Winter term.

An analysis of natural and experimental groups from a social structural view. The study of processes of differentiation, integration, power, etc., internally; and of nesting of small groups in larger collectives. Prerequisite: 3rd or 4th year standing in a social science or by permission. 3 hour seminar, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 315
courses.title: Social Stratification
paras: Analysis of social classes in society including their basis for development, composition, and consequences for society. Special attention is given to social stratification in Canada. Prerequisite: Soc. 101 *. 3 lectures, Fail term.

courses.label: SOC 321
courses.title: Research Methods 1
paras: A systematic treatment of the logic and practice of methods basic to social research. Emphasis is on problems of research design based on the analysis of case studies. Special attention is given to problems of participant observation, use of available data, measurement of variables, and simple multivariate analysis. Students will be given laboratory and field experience in several techniques of research. Special attention is given to Canadian cases and data. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, I hour lab., Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 322
courses.title: Research Methods 2
paras: Continuation of Research Methods 1. Includes an introduction to sampling, scaling, the analysis of change, and experimental design. Students will be asked to construct a research design for the study of a theoreticaliy relevant problem in sociology. Prerequisite: Sociology 321* 2 lectures, 1 hour lab, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 323
courses.title: Project in Sociological Research 24* Field Research in Canadian Institutions
paras: Introduction to sociological research through the formation of a theoretically based research objective and its implementation in a small scale team research project. Students must be willing to participate in team research with 6 - 8 other students. Readings are assigned that relate to the steps in the team project. The course grade is based on each team’s final project report and on a final examination covering the readings. Prerequisite: Soc. 101*. 2 hour seminar, Winter term.

A study of selected institution in the local community, such as the Courts, Mass Media, and Labour Unions, will be conducted employing observational and interview procedures. Prerequisite: consent of the instructor. 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 330
courses.title: Comparative Social Structure
paras: General theoretical and methodological issues facing comparative sociology; comparative methods at work in the treatment of Western and non-western societies (including Canada). Prerequisite: Soc. 101 *. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 331
courses.title: Theories of Social Change
paras: A systematic review and analysis of major theories of social change including some of the classical and modern theories. Analysis will focus upon the sources, patterns, processes and consequences of change. Special topics to be included are: Marxism, social change in developing countries, the role of ideas, and the breakdown and reorganization of social structure. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 332
courses.title: Social Conflict and Modernization
paras: This course constitutes a sociological study of violent and nonviolent conflict and modernization in comparative perspective. A critical review of the selected theoretical explanations of collective protest and social change will be done to discover linkage between social conflict and modernization. An attempt will be made to examine causes and consequences of racial and political violence in modernizing society. Prerequisite: Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 334
courses.title: Northern Lands and Peoples
paras: A comparative study of social and cultural change in Arctic and Sub-arctic areas brought about by political and economic development of those lands. No prerequisites. $45.00 fee to cover field trip. 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 338
courses.title: Sociology of Literature
paras: This course attempts to provide the student with an opportunity for exploring literature as a social phenomenon. Specific areas to be dealt with might include: 1) the relationship of the artist to his social structure; 2) the nature of the relationship of the work and its audience; 3) the attitudes toward the social structure implicit in the work of art. In general the course is viewed as an attempt to combine both the scientific approach and the humanistic approach to literature. Here literature is viewed as including both belles lettres and popular culture. The course will be taught by someone in Sociology and someone in Literature in dialogue method. Prerequisite: Sociology 101* and English 101 (or equivalent). 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 339
courses.title: Industrial Sociology
paras: Sociological analysis of industry, including relationships between labour and management and industry and society. Prerequisites: Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Fall term.
Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: SOC 340
courses.title: Formal Organizations
paras: A survey of theory and research on formal organizations making use of selected contributions from the scientific management and human relations approaches, but with emphasis on the structure and functions of large scale organizations. The nature and types of formal organizations; contro] techniques and leadership; relations of the organization to its clients and publics; informal aspects of the organization; organizational tensions and pathologies of bureaucratic systems; how the organization adjusts to change. Prerequisite: Soc. 101* 2 hour seminar, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 341
courses.title: Sociology of Occupations
paras: The sociological study of occupations as an aid to understanding the social structure; social and demographic aspects of the labour force; the meaning of work; the relation of work and leisure; career and occupational mobility patterns; occupation and status; professionalization; trends in occupations. Prerequisite: Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 350
courses.title: Seminar in Socialization Processes
paras: The social creation of Actors; the establishment of legitimacy and the development of loyalty; socialization through the life cycle; cohorts and age-grading; generational differences and youth movements. Prerequisite: 3rd or 4th year standing in a social science or by permission. 3 hour seminar, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 355
courses.title: Sociology of Religion
paras: The analysis of religion as a social institution; its relationship to culture, personality and social change with consideration given to theories of religious behaviour and contemporary research findings. Prerequisite: Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 360
courses.title: Political Sociology
paras: The sociological analysis of the institutionalization of power, political movements, parties, conflict and its accomodation. Prerequisite. Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 365
courses.title: Social Structure of the Soviet Union
paras: A sociological analysis of contemporary Soviet society focusing on the patterns and functions of its basic institutions including the family, government, education, and industry, consideration of class formation and distribution of power. No prerequisites. 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 372
courses.title: Medical Sociology
paras: Examination of the medical care structures from the point of view of patients, health care professionals in the system, and systems analysis. Structures of interest are primary health care settings, hospitals, and professional associations. Emphasis on cross-cultural comparisons and changes over time as well as critical analysis of current structure from the point of view of the Canadian health care consumer. Prerequisite: Soc. 101*. 2 lectures, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 382
courses.title: Techniques of Demographic Analysis
paras: Introduction to the standard techniques of analysis of enumeration and registration data. Prerequisite: Soc. 261 *. J lecture, 2 hour lab, winter term.

courses.label: SOC 400
courses.title: Processes of Planned Change
paras: The goal of the course is to develop models of social change, through active participation in action groups in the community, reading, seminars, and written analyses. All students will be expected to join a group oriented to altering or maintaining existing social structures, to participate as full members, and at the same time to make social scientific sense of social process as manifested in the group and its relation to the environing system. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor. 2 hour seminar.

courses.label: SOC 402
courses.title: Marxist Social Theory
paras: This course will focus on the contribution of Marxism to the development of sociological theory in its relation to other types of social thought. Readings will include selections from Marx, Engels, Lenin, Gramsci, Plekhanov, Lukacs, and contemporary sources. Prerequisite: 4th year Honours or graduate standing. 2 hour seminar, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 410
courses.title: Seminar in Self and Social Interaction
paras: Social Psychological theory and research on the self, self-awareness, and self-worth; the self in systems of social interaction. Prerequisite: 3rd or 4th year standing in a social science or by permission. 3 hour seminar, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 415
courses.title: Seminar in Sociology of Women
paras: An examination of selected areas of contemporary sociological theory with respect to their treatment of women. Prerequisite: Soc. 215 and 3rd or 4th year standing in Sociology. 2 hour seminar, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 421
courses.title: Secondary Analysis of Survey Data
paras: Methodological problems in developing and testing social and behavioural theory through the analysis of survey data will be examined, and actual analysis of data from local data banks will be performed, using available computer programs. A term paper consisting of an original analysis and interpretation will be required. No previous experience with the computer is assumed. Prerequisite: Soc. 202* or permission of instructor. 2 hour seminar, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 425
courses.title: The Development of Sociological Theory
paras: Development of sociological theory in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Emphasis is on the European tradition although selective attention is given to North American theorists. Prerequisite: Open only to students in Sociology. 2 lectures, Fail term.

courses.label: SOC 426
courses.title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
paras: The development of sociological theory in the 20th century. Included is discussion of current theoretical work. Prerequisite: Open only to students in Sociology. 2 lectures, Winter term.
Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: SOC 432
courses.title: The Sociology of Political Knowledge
paras: This seminar will undertake to develop a general theory of the sociological roots and implications of political thought in relation to contemporary social movements and ideologies in historical perspective. Comparative illustrative materials will be drawn from Latin America, Europe, Africa and/or Asia, which will also serve as a basis for research papers. Prerequisite: any I of the following Soc. 241*, 331*, 360*, 425*, and Honours Soc. and/or Political Science or graduate standing. 2 hour seminar, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 451
courses.title: Seminar: Problems in Contemporary Theory and Research
paras: Examinations of current frames of reference and theories in sociology and related disciplines. Their utility in sociological problem formulation and their test by current methods and techniques. Prerequisite: 3rd or 4th year Honours. 3 hour seminar, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 466
courses.title: Reading 1
paras: Selected readings and essay asssignments under the direction of a faculty member. Prerequisite: 3rd or 4th year standing in Sociology and permission of the instructor. Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 467
courses.title: Reading 2 ‘0 Seminar: Practicum in Theory and Methodology
paras: Selected readings and essay assignments under the direction of a faculty member. Prerequisite: 3rd or 4th year standing in Sociology and permission of the instructor. Winter term. A preparation for advanced undergraduate students for an independent, sophisticated orientation to graduate study. The practicum provides opportunities for: 1) developing research designs on the basis of extant theory, and 2) theorizing on the basis of the reanalysis and reinterpretation of extant data. Prerequisites: 4th year Honours or equivalent. 2 hour seminar.

courses.label: SOC 480
courses.title: Advanced Social Statistics
paras: Multiple and partial correlation; regression; analysis of variance and covariance; selected non-parametric techniques. Prerequisite: Sociology 202* or equivalent. 2 lectures, 1 hour lab, Winter term.

courses.label: SOC 481
courses.title: Mathematical Sociology
paras: Selected mathematical techniques with applications to sociology; sets and graphs, Markov chains and game theory. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. 2 lectures, Fall term.

courses.label: SOC 499
courses.title: Senior Honours Essay
paras: Required of all honours students in Sociology or by election by joint honours students in their fourth year. For students electing Honours Sociology (Canadian Studies) the essay should bear on some topic of particular sociological significance for Canadian Society. Prerequisite: 4th year Honours.

courses.label: SOC 542
courses.title: Department of Sociology and Anthropology
paras: The following courses are administered by Conrad Grebel College

courses.label: SOC 207
courses.title: G Educational Sociology
paras: This course is designed for co-op and regular students who plan to enter the teaching field. Attention will be focused on the concepts and theories of sociology as they apply especially to the educational system. Winter Term.

courses.label: SOC 230
courses.title: G Family and Kinship
paras: An evaluation of the origin and growth of the family as a social institution; its structures and functions in primitive and modern societies; the effect of modern technology on the family, trends and contemporary problems.

courses.label: SOC 307
courses.title: G Problems in Contemporary Education 370*G Sociology of Law
paras: An examination of intentional communities; extinct and contemporary. Attention will be paid to origin, purpose, structure and process in each community studied. An assessment of factors contributing to success and failure will be attempted.

A study of problems arising from the interplay between institutionalized education and the forces of rapid social change in the contemporary society; the clash of value systems of youth and the “establishment”. It emphasizes the changing concepts of the roles of the learners and instructors, social dimensions of newer learning theories and educational programmes arising therefrom, goals of formal education, decision making processes within educational organizations, obsolescence of some of the traditional patterns of formal education, and like topics. Themes will be selected and studied in depth on a seminar basis.

An overview of the major trends in the sociology of law since World War II. Consideration will be given to contributions of legal scholars as well as of social scientists. Special attention will be paid to the growing public awareness of the failure of law in Canadian society to provide adequate justice or social control in a growing number of situations. Investigations of concrete issues, such as the jury system, courts, police and mass media, will be an integral part of the course. Fall term.
The following courses are administered by Renison College

courses.label: SOC 120R
courses.title: Fundamentals of Sociology
paras: Survey of key topics and study of the basic skills, concepts and interests comprising the sociologist’s tools of analysis. The course will include social organization, culture, socialization, primary groups, social stratification and associations.

courses.label: SOC 220R
courses.title: Sociological Analysis
paras: Applying sociological analysis to three selected areas: the major institutions of education, religion and law, and developing a pattern and an approach which would be applied to the study of other social areas.

courses.label: SOC 221R
courses.title: Master Trends in Modern Society
paras: Introducing the student to the main ideas of urban, industrial and political sociology studied within a context emphasizing social change; illustrations will be drawn from emergent as well as advanced societies.
Department of Sociology and Anthropology

courses.label: SOC 225R
courses.title: Race and Culture in the Third World 1
paras: A general introduction to the contemporary problems of race, culture and ethnic relations in the developing countries of Asia and Africa. An analysis of historic, geographic, cultural and socio-economic background of selected societies.

courses.label: SOC 226R
courses.title: Race and Culture in the Third World 2
paras: An introduction to the problems of acculteration as well as intergroup relations in plural societies in selected areas in the Caribbean, South and Southeast Asia, East and Southern Africa.
The following course is administered by St. Jerome’s College

courses.label: SOC 232J
courses.title: The Family and Society
paras: The course is designed essentially to assess the role of the family in society. This will be done primarily on the basis of an analysis of the institutions of the family and marriage on a cross cultural basis. The universality of the family has always been proclaimed by Anthropologists. This view will be challenged in the light of relatively recent ethnographic materials which tend to establish the fact that this proclaimed universality is not absolute. The biological basis of the family will be examined in some detail, and an attempt will be made to establish the family as a biosocial unit. Courtship, mate selection and divorce, as well as a brief overview of human sexuality and the role of sex in marriage and family stability will be examined. Prerequisite: Sociology 101* or permission of the instructor. 3 hours, lectures and tutorial. (not offered in 1972-73)

Undergraduate Courses

courses.label: SOC 111
courses.title: Calculus 1 (formerly SD110)
paras: Functions and limits. The derivative and differentiation formulas. Extrema. Antiderivatives. The definite integral, integration as the limit of a sum and fundamental theorem of integral calculus. Areas. Transcendental functions. Integration. Introduction to partial differentiation. Optimization: unconstrained, constrained with equations and constrained with inequalities. Selected applications.

courses.label: SOC 112
courses.title: Calculus 2 (formerly SD111)
paras: Analytic geometry in three-dimensional space. Infinite series. Multiple integrals. Differentiation of an integral, with applications (i.e. optimization of an expected value of a function in statistical models) Partial differentiation. Introduction to Differential Equations.
13 Finite Mathematics (formerly SD112)
Department of Systems Design
Symbolic logic, set theory, permutations, combinations, discrete probability theory.

courses.label: SOC 114
courses.title: Theory and Applications of Probability (formerly SD215)
paras: Sample spaces and probability measures. Random variables. Independent events. Probability density and cumulative distribution functions. Presentation of discrete and continuous probability density functions (Binomial, Normal, etc.). Moments of a distribution. Characteristic functions. Multivariate distributions. Marginal distributions. Transformations of random variables which will involve: distributions of functions of random variables and their sums. Laws of large numbers. Central limit theory. Selected applications.

courses.label: SOC 115
courses.title: Linear Algebra (formerly SD113)
paras: Finite dimensional vector spaces. Linear dependence. The concept of basis. Orthogonalization of vectors. Methods of changing the basis. Matrices and determinants. Systems of linear equations and inequalities. The linear programming problem and solution by simplex method. Linear transformations. Matrices as linear transformation.

courses.label: SOC 121
courses.title: Digital Computation 1 (formerly SD120)
paras: Introduction to electronic digital computers; hardware and software organization, basic features of Fortran, examples of efficient algorithms for engineering computations.

courses.label: SOC 132
courses.title: Engineering Economics (formerly SD130)
paras: Cost-benefit analysis, critical path methods, interest, project economics, decision making, utility theory, project organizational theory.

courses.label: SOC 151
courses.title: Physics 1 (formerly SD150)
paras: Statics of particles, vectors, equilibrium of+rigid bodies, centroids, the analysis of structures, forces in beams and cables, friction and moments of inertia.

courses.label: SOC 152
courses.title: Physics 2 (formerly SD151)
paras: Rectilinear motion, plane motion, dynamics of particles, work and energy, linear momentum, rotational motion, angular momentum, harmonic motion, gravitational, wave motion, sound waves.

courses.label: SOC 162
courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Design (formerly SD160)
paras: An introductory course on the principles of engineering design culminating in a project involving the solution of a relevant need. Specific topics introduced are: The systems approach, principles of planning, the statement of a design problem and the flow of information. Innovation and the creation of design solutions, physical, economic and financial feasibility, solution evaluation and selection. Value and utility, simulation, modelling and optimization.

courses.label: SOC 181
courses.title: Graphics (formerly SD180) 001, 002 Focal Issues In Contemporary Society (these purses also listed as Arts 120*G, Arts 121*G)
paras: A course in fundamentals of graphics with emphasis on basic techniques required for visual communication and computation.

An attempt to bring together and condense what are believed to be essential elements of the several social science disciplines. The core of the study that will be used is a group of selected contemporary issues with implications that cut across all the various disciplines. Some effort will be made to discuss values deemed appropriate for our age. Integrating universal concepts or problems to be dealt with are: personality, work, community, and society.

courses.label: SOC 211
courses.title: Theory and applications of Statistics (formerly SD216)
paras: Sample statistics and their distributions. Order statistics and their distributions. Decision making under uncertainty. Statistical inference: Estimation and testing statistical hypothesis. The 1 theory of the least Se ee ee ce. oe erase Me wee nnn

courses.label: SOC 212
courses.title: Applicable Mathematics for Systems Design
paras: Topics from differential calculus, partial differential equations; line, surface and volume integrals; functions of the complex variable, Taylor & Laurent series, Cauchy’s integral formula; operational calculus, Laplace Transforms theory; Introduction to Vector calculus and certain special functions.

courses.label: SOC 213
courses.title: Differential Equations (formerly SD217)
paras: Exact equations, integrating factor, separation of variables. Linear equations with constant coefficients, simultaneous equations, Laplace transform, solution by series. Non-linear differential equations and computer methods. Introduction to difference equations.

courses.label: SOC 222
courses.title: Numerical Analysis and Computation (formerly SD221)
paras: Application of digital’ computers to the solution of equations; determinants and matrices; eigenvalue problems, numerical solution of ordinary differential equations; difference equations, numerical integration methods; error analysis.

courses.label: SOC 231
courses.title: Micro-Economic Analysis and Policy
paras: Analysis of public and private choices among users of scarce resources. The interaction of choices to form micro systems. Examples of policy questions; costs and benefits of alternative methods of pollution control, pricing of private and public goods.

courses.label: SOC 241
courses.title: Human Systems Engineering 1
paras: The structure and function of man in relation to systems design; the relationship of biology and human physiology to engineering; biological concepts, biological variation. Introductory concepts in molecular biology and genetics; the cell as a micro-system; the role of water transport; man as a complex of systems and subsystems; the nature of selected subsystems (including introduction to electrophysiology).

courses.label: SOC 242
courses.title: Human Systems Engineering 2
paras: The attributes of man as a functioning system; the nature of human sensory and perceptual processes; memory, learning and the application of information theory to human information processing; arousal and motivation; intelligence, learning and cognitive processes; motor function; the nature of human work, skill and fatigue.

courses.label: SOC 252
courses.title: Physical Systems 1 (formerly SD251)
paras: Component models, interconnection models, system equations and their tank properties and solutions. These concepts are developed with respect to electrical systems.

courses.label: SOC 261
courses.title: Systems Design Workshop 1
paras: A problem and project oriented course wherein emphasis is placed on designing and presenting creative solutions to real-life problems. The problems are selected to cover all disciplines to which the student

courses.label: SOC 262
courses.title: Systems Design Workshop 2
paras: becomes exposed each year. Both the problems and the students work are expected to increase in sophistication and complexity in accordance with the student’s progress through the course.

courses.label: SOC 281
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electric charge, Coulomb’s Law of Electrostatic Forces; Electric Fields, Gauss’ Law, conductors and electric fields; Electric Potential; Capacitance, dielectrics. Magnetic fields, flux of magnetic induction; current, resistance and electric circuits; Induced EMF, inductance, Lenz’s law, Faraday’s law; magnetism in matter, transformers, motors, generators, introduction to basic electronic devices.

courses.label: SOC 282
courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids
paras: Statics and resistance of materials. Equilibrium of particles, rigid bodies and deformable bodies. Vector fields. Bay systems. Stress-strain relationships. Elastic and inelastic behaviour of prismatic members subjected to axial, shearing, torsional and flexural deformations.

courses.label: SYDE 291
courses.title: Systems Design Laboratory 1
paras: An integrated laboratory sequence stressing instrumentation and measurement techniques.
292 Systems Design Laboratory 2

courses.label: SYDE 311
courses.title: Operations Research 1 (formerly SD334)
paras: Introduction and background to the application of scientific models to the study of operational problem. This course is intended to present an integrated view of the “deterministic operations research models”. Topics will include: mathematical techniques of unconstrained and constrained optimization, followed by the construction, evaluation and applicability of various models in allocation, inventory, replacement, sequencing and related problems.

courses.label: SYDE 312
courses.title: Operations Research 2 (formerly SD414)
paras: A continuation of SD311, with emphasis on Stochastic Operations Research Models. Topics will include: Decision making under uncertainty, Queuing models and related probabilistic techniques, feed back control, probabilistic inventory, competitive strategies and related topics.

courses.label: SYDE 322
courses.title: Computer Simulation of Systems
paras: System modelling, discrete and continuous system models; system simulation techniques, digital computer methods, fundamentals of analog computation, time and magnitude scaling; analog computer simulation methods; digital simulation of analog computers; block oriented languages; advantages and disadvantages of digital and analog simulation techniques, introduction to system simulation using hybrid computers.

courses.label: SYDE 331
courses.title: Conflict Analysis (formerly SD336)
paras: The application for non-quantitative game+theory to the analysis of conflict, particularly conflicts arising in the implementation of design projects, the general characteristics (through Metagame theory) and specific applied techniques for analyzing conflicts between parties each with separate objectives.

courses.label: SYDE 333
courses.title: Experimental Design
paras: Optimum seeking methods: analysis of experimental optimum-seeking techniques. Studies include deterministic and stochastic problems. Topics include; single variable search, simultaneous and sequential search, geometry of multidimensional response surfaces and methods of steepest ascent; regression analysis with a systematic treatment of the analysis of multiple classifications involving fixed and random effects and crossed and nested variables of classification. Applications of statistical methods to the efficient design of industrial experiments with considerations to suitability.

courses.label: SYDE 334
courses.title: Metagame Analysis
paras: Model building techniques for analysing conflict situations, using inputs from the social sciences and operations research.

courses.label: SYDE 341
courses.title: Human Engineering and Rational Design
paras: The man-machine interface; communication and the design of displays (visual, auditory, kinesthetic, tactile, etc.); human motor activities, speed, accuracy, strength and force; functional operation and the design of controls; illumination, colour, and design of workplaces.

courses.label: SYDE 342
courses.title: Problems of Man in the Operational Environment (formerly SD343)
paras: The man-machine-environment complex; the nature of the operational environment; neuroendocrine system and the non-specific response to stress (adaptation); specific effects, hazards, and management of specific forms of stress, e.g. acoustic noise, heat and cold, toxic materials, etc.

courses.label: SYDE 351
courses.title: Physical Systems 2 (formerly SD353)
paras: The subject matter is similar to SD252 except that the development is based on other physical systems such as structural and hydraulic systems.

courses.label: SYDE 353
courses.title: Time Domain Models for Physical Systems
paras: State equations for two-terminal component systems; time varying and non-linear components; analytical solutions for state models, numerical and analogue methods for solution.

courses.label: SYDE 354
courses.title: Algorithms for Computer-Aided System Analysis
paras: Techniques for tree selection, manipulation of topological information, evaluation of the exponential function of a matrix, etc. The emphasis is on the algorithms but students will be expected to implement them on the computer. The course includes a survey of the capabilities of existing programmes for system analysis.
361 Systems Design Workshop 3
A continuation of the Systems Design Workshop for third year students.
362 Systems Design Workshop 4

courses.label: SYDE 371
courses.title: Introduction to Human Communication Systems
paras: The course focuses upon a variety of communication systems including man-man, man-machine and machine-machine systems. Various models of communication systems will be examined paying particular attention to the assumptions and situational factors upon which the models are based. Using a systems approach such concepts as redundancy, entropy, feedback, openness-closedness, equi-finality, nonsummativity, homeostasis and stability, etc., will be examined.

courses.label: SYDE 381
courses.title: Materials Engineering
paras: A general introduction to the science of materials: so providing a basic understanding of the scientific principles involved and an introduction to the wide variety of materials available to the designer today. To demonstrate some of the important relationships existing between the structure of a material and its properties, and to consider some of the ways in which materials are shaped, formed and fabricated into articles for our everyday use.

courses.label: SYDE 382
courses.title: Applied Electronics (formerly SD381)
paras: Component models of various electronic devices, oscillation, amplification, modulation, detection, application to instrumentation.

courses.label: SYDE 384
courses.title: Thermodynamics (GE31)
paras: The scope and limitations of thermodynamics. Macroscopic approach to energy, work and the First Law. Introduction to statistical thermodynamics and the microscopic description of energy, work and the First Law. The fundamental energy equation. The Second Law of Thermodynamics, principle of increase of entropy, limiting cycle efficiencies, criteria for equilibrium. Thermodynamic potentials. Irreversibility, friction, and availability. Phase equilibrium, phase change, mixtures. The steady flow energy equation and applications. The evaluation of state functions.

courses.label: SYDE 391
courses.title: Systems Design Laboratory 3
paras: A continuation of SD291/292 for third year students.

courses.label: SYDE 392
courses.title: Systems Design Laboratory 4
paras: Department of Systems Design

courses.label: SYDE 411
courses.title: Operations Research 3
paras: Readings suited to individual interests of the students and aimed at solving special project problems which the student may select.
421 Computer Aided Design (formerly SD323) 32 Macro-Economics and Public Policy (formerly SD433)
The design process; computer-oriented system models; simulation languages for continuous and discrete systems; man-machine interaction; design of problem-oriented computer language.

The functioning of National and Regional economics. The relations between the behaviour of classes of decision-making units and the performance of the economic system. Examples of policy questions; costs and benefits of alternative methods of attaining price stability. Full employment and economic growth.

courses.label: SYDE 434
courses.title: Policy Studies
paras: The combined use of model-building techniques and social science methods in approaching real-world problems.

courses.label: SYDE 451
courses.title: Multi-terminal Representations and Piecewise Analysis of Physical Systems
paras: Multi-terminal representations, coupled 2-terminal components, tree transformations, solution of large systems through sub-systems, two-ports and their interconnection, equivalent 2-terminal component systems.

courses.label: SYDE 452
courses.title: Introduction to Linear Control Systems
paras: Application of Systems theory to the problems of control. The course integrates this study with an exposition of classical control theory.
453 Power Systems 1
Applicaton of systems theory to large power distribution networks and electromechanical energy conversion systems.

courses.label: SYDE 454
courses.title: Hydraulic Systems
paras: Application of systems theory to the analysis of hydraulic systems; particular emphasis is given to the analysis and design of fluid distribution systems.

courses.label: SYDE 455
courses.title: Transportation Systems
paras: Application of Systems theory to the analysis of urban and inter-urban traffic systems and to combined air, land and sea transportation systems.

courses.label: SYDE 461
courses.title: Systems Design Workshop 5
paras: A continuation of the Systems Design Workshop for fourth year students. The emphasis will be on an individual problem chosen from the student’s technical option area.

courses.label: SYDE 471
courses.title: Communication Media
paras: The course encompasses the tools of communication and the nature and use of communication media. There will be a particular emphasis on those media containing a large technological component; machine-mediated human communication systems, e.g. computer graphics, film, T.V., etc.

courses.label: SYDE 473
courses.title: Intercultural Communication 15 Man-Machine Communication Systems
paras: The problems of designing a human communication system where more than one culture is involved. Anthropological, sociological, psychological, political, economic and technological aspects of such design. Environmental perception, value systems, social forms, etc.

The nature and design of machine-mediated human communication systems. Consideration will be given to displays, computer graphics, computer-aided instruction and mass communication media (Film, T.V., radio, print). The design of new media innovation. A system approach will be adopted with special attention to the socio-economic effects of such systems.

courses.label: SYDE 511
courses.title: Linear Graph Theory
paras: Fundamental definitions, properties of circuits, paths in a graph, and Euler graphs. Properties of cutsets. Matrix representation of linear graphs and trees. Planar graphs and their duals. Nonplanar graphs, pseudo cuts and duals. Oriented graphs.

courses.label: SYDE 512
courses.title: Applications of Linear Graph Theory
paras: Topological formulas for general linear systems, synthesis of communication nets, system diagnosis. Applications to switching theory, sociology, economics, etc.

courses.label: SYDE 513
courses.title: Mathematical Programming
paras: Theory and application of linear programming techniques: simplex, the transportation and assignment problems, duality and degeneracy. Industrial application$ to production and inventory control. Selected problems from nonlinear and dynamic programming.

courses.label: SYDE 514
courses.title: Multivariate Statistics
paras: Applications of econometric models, regression analysis, factor analysis, Statistical decision theory, and other methods and models for the policy analysis of socio-economic systems. Selected references will be assigned.

courses.label: SYDE 515
courses.title: Networks and Combinatories
paras: The emphasis in this course will be the use of combinatorial and graph-theoretic methods for operations research. Topics will include “Advanced PERT and CPM”, scheduling and routing, graph theoretic methods for socio-economic systems.

courses.label: SYDE 521
courses.title: Analog and Hybrid Computing Systems
paras: Theory and operation of analog computers; parallel logic; digitally simulated analog computers; introduction to hybrid computing.

courses.label: SYDE 522
courses.title: Computer-Aided Design 2
paras: A detailed study of two major simulation languages, one continuous (CSMP or equivalent) and one discrete-event (GPSS or equivalent). Simulation projects.

courses.label: SYDE 533
courses.title: Production and Inventory Control
paras: The objective of the course is to study the nature, problems and techniques of planning and control. Topics: influence of forecasting, inventory managment, planning, scheduling, despatching and performance evaluation. Analytic techniques pertaining to these areas are introduced.

courses.label: SYDE 534
courses.title: Planning of Facilities
paras: Industrial and Non-Industrial facilities. Networks, locational analysis, physical layout and spatial analysis, allocation of facilities, criteria for optimality, utilization and occupation, various operations research techniques for the analysis and synthesis of networks of facilities, on-the-job machine problem.

courses.label: SYDE 535
courses.title: Queuing Models
paras: Definition of a queuing process; explicit solution of queuing problems when arrival and service distribution are exponential. Examination of special problems for general arrival and service distributions. Multiserverproblems; queues in series, bulk service and other types of service discipline.

courses.label: SYDE 536
courses.title: Economic Planning Models
paras: Simple dynamic models, static and dynamic Leontief systems, welfare economics, capital investment and project evaluation models, applications to problems of cost-benefit analysis and public enterprises, portfolio selection models and game theoretic models in economics.

courses.label: SYDE 538
courses.title: Special Topics in Operations Research
paras: Given by a guest lecturer. The contents of this course will vary according to the available guest.
Department of Systems Design

courses.label: SYDE 541
courses.title: The Ergonomics of Special Environments
paras: Effects, hazards and managment of sustained acceleration, weightlessness, vibration and impact acceleration (with specific reference to aviation, spaceflight, and automotive safety); effects, hazards, and management of exposure to low and high barometric pressure (with specific reference to human problems at altitude, and to underwater engineering).

courses.label: SYDE 542
courses.title: Human Engineering and Systems Development
paras: Human function in systems; man’s capacities and limitations as a component of a complex system; assignment of operations to man and machine; equipment design in relation to human capacity; training programmes, procedures, and devices; task description and analysis; analytic methods for test and evaluation in human engineering.
343 Human Engineering (formerly SD501) $44 Ergonomics (formerly SD502)
Man-machine systems; man-machine interface; presentation of information; design of displays and controls; workplace layout, human factors in design.

Significance of ergonomics; man-machine-environment complex; physiology of work, fatigue, and boredom; environmental factors in industry (noise, vibration, vision, illumination, heat, cold, toxic chemicals, radiation); industrial, and automotive safety.

courses.label: SYDE 552
courses.title: Power Systems 2
paras: A continuation of SD453 with emphasis on load flow, system stability, operation under imbalanced conditions, fault detection.

courses.label: SYDE 563
courses.title: Aesthetic and Perceptual Aspects of Design
paras: Presentation and discussion of appropriate and possible methods for design of systems or artifacts in which aesthetic characteristics and visual form are primary requirements of the design.

courses.label: SYDE 564
courses.title: Methodological Processes in Design
paras: Presentation and discussion of appropriate and possible methods for the design of systems or artifacts in which manufacturing processes, material properties and distribution processes constrain the design.
